• Adobe and Google are expanding their partnership: Google models inside Adobe tools, and DeepMind collaborating on Photoshop image editing.

• Macro Chat agents can join channels like teammates and listen ambiently.
• Product Hunt MCP server lets Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and ChatGPT search launches and draft submissions.
• Scubiee: a free, open-source local context engine for 13+ coding agents.

Gemini is omitted from m4lka’s 6-seat framework because that specific architecture was designed exclusively for xAI’s Grok Bot ecosystem (using tools like Dr. Eggbot, Grok Desktop, and Grok 4.7). In that model, the 6 core roles operate entirely within the Grok workspace:

[ CHIEF ] ──> [ OPS ] ──> [ CHECKER ] ──> [ SPECIALISTS (2) ] ──> [ MISC ]
However, if you apply this exact 6-seat blueprint to RDS RevOps (https://t.co/NgzDhkWWB6) while keeping Gemini in the architecture, Gemini takes on critical high-value roles to maximize efficiency and minimize cost:

Where Gemini Fits in the 6-Seat Architecture

[ CHIEF SEAT ]
            Grok 4.7 / Grok App ($30/mo Capped)
                - Front Door & Routing Only
                             │
                             ▼
                        [ OPS SEAT ]
                  Meta Muse (Free Cron)
                - State Board & Timed Sweeps
                             │
            ┌────────────────┴────────────────┐
            ▼                                 ▼
   [ CHECKER SEAT ]                 [ SPECIALIST SEATS ]
  Gemini 3.1 Pro / Live           Gemini 3.8 / 3.7 Flash
- Verification & Multimodal Gate   - High-Speed Execution & RAG
- Halts non-reversible actions     - Neon Postgres pgvector Context

Gemini’s Dedicated Roles in the Stack

1. The CHECKER Seat (Gemini 3.1 Pro / Multimodal Live API)

Role: Proof-Before-Trust Gatekeeper.
Why Gemini: Gemini’s long context window and native multimodal audio/visual capabilities make it an ideal choice for the Checker.
Execution: Before any output is marked "Done" on the board, Gemini audits execution logs, verifies code changes, or evaluates user UI assets. Because it only runs at the gate, token consumption stays locked to verification calls rather than open chat loops.
2. The SPECIALIST Seats (Gemini 3.8 / 3.7 Flash)
Role: Domain Execution (Support, Data Analysis, RevOps Workflows).
Why Gemini: At $0.75 / 1M input tokens (and up to 90% savings on cached inputs), Gemini Flash is significantly cheaper for routine micro-tasks than running standard Grok models for every worker.
Execution: Gemini Flash receives clean, single-task payloads from the Ops board, runs the retrieval or code modification, updates Neon Postgres (pgvector), and immediately terminates—preventing token re-read leakage.
Integrated Flat-Rate & API Hybrid Stack
SeatAssigned Tool / ModelCost StructurePrimary JobChiefGrok App / Grok 4.7Capped UI Plan ($30/mo)Front-door routing, prompt strategy, and human interaction.OpsMeta Muse / Vercel CronFree TierTimed Cron routines, board updates, zero active polling.CheckerGemini 3.1 ProMetered Gate (Pennies/run)Verifies proof (./verify check), reviews UI/code, halts risky actions.Specialist 1Gemini 3.8 FlashBilled at $0.75/1M InputFast vector retrieval (pgvector) and structured payload generation.Specialist 2Cursor IDEIncluded in WorkspaceCodebase updates, local linting, and automated PR checks.Miscgrok-build-0.1 / FlashLightweight APICaptures random requests to prevent polluting Specialist memory.
Cost Optimization Strategy for https://t.co/NgzDhkWWB6
Never use Gemini as the Chief router: Keep conversational chit-chat inside the flat-rate Grok UI or Cursor workspace to protect against API context bloat.
Assign Gemini to stateless Specialist tasks: Pass structured JSON tasks to Gemini Flash so it operates on fresh input contexts every run, keeping total API spend near zero.
Use Gemini Pro exclusively for verification: Run the Checker seat on Gemini Pro only when a task reaches the "Ready for Review" state on the board.

note_tweet.text:
I rebuilt ResearchMind so a research draft has to show its evidence, or stay provisional.

The first version was a Streamlit app: Search, Reader, Writer, and Critic, running in sequence, with state in the browser session. The critic was another model pass, not a check against stored passages.

The upgrade is a public Research Console. You ask one public question, watch a bounded LangGraph workflow (plan, at most two workers, sources, evidence, verify, report, review), then open the report and the evidence ledger. If claims cannot be grounded, the answer is labeled provisional and the gaps stay visible.

What changed versus that first post:
• React console on Vercel, instead of Streamlit
• FastAPI + LangGraph, with durable jobs and guest quotas in Neon Postgres
• Live progress over SSE that can be replayed after a refresh
• LiteLLM routing on a free-model allowlist, with no automatic paid fallback (an optional Meta last-resort hop runs only after free routes fail)
• A thin Cloudflare MCP worker that forwards tools to the API
• Offline DeepEval on 20 hand-built synthetic fixtures (not live accuracy, not a V1 vs V2 comparison): Faithfulness 0.925 (n=20) and Answer relevancy 0.700 (n=20), judged by meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor, plus a 20/20 deterministic fixture self-check

This is still a student portfolio demo. One research run per guest identity. Render Free can take about a minute to wake. SSRF is not fully closed. Those fixture scores are not a claim that the live system is 93% accurate.

Try the console: https://t.co/3TFnhK5WRy
Code: https://t.co/bca3oqBB60

If you were reviewing this, what would you want next: a V1 vs V2 eval on frozen sources, or tighter live-provider reliability?

#LangGraph #FastAPI #SystemDesign #SoftwareEngineering
